s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive neurological disorder with autonomic dysfunction and cognitive decline
key_facts: 3-year history of progressive disorder
Denies paresthesias, dysesthesias, or loss of sensation
Abnormal cardiac parasympathetic function without orthostatic hypotension
Patchy decrease in sweat output on quantitative sudomotor axon reflex test
Near complete global anhidrosis on thermoregulatory sweat test
Low α-galactosidase activity (0.056 U/L)
Elevated protein levels in cerebrospinal fluid (95 mg/dL)
No pleocytosis in cerebrospinal fluid
Bilateral hyperintensity in the pulvinar region of thalami on MRI Brain
Global diffuse brain volume loss on MRI Brain
Positive for pseudo-α-galactosidase allele
Mild neurocognitive and memory deficits on neuropsychological testing

raw.rationale: The combination of progressive disorder, autonomic dysfunction (abnormal cardiac parasympathetic function and anhidrosis), ataxia, and cognitive decline without significant sensory symptoms, along with the imaging findings of bilateral hyperintensity in the pulvinar region of thalami and global diffuse brain volume loss, are highly suggestive of Multiple System Atrophy.

rejected.label: Fabry Disease
rejected.why: Low α-galactosidase activity is consistent with Fabry Disease, but the absence of paresthesias, dysesthesias, or loss of sensation and the specific pattern of autonomic dysfunction and imaging findings are more characteristic of Multiple System Atrophy.

rejected.label: Frontotemporal Dementia
rejected.why: While cognitive decline is present, the prominent autonomic dysfunction, ataxia, and specific imaging findings are not typical of Frontotemporal Dementia.

rejected.label: Late-Onset Tay-Sachs Disease
rejected.why: This condition typically presents with motor symptoms and cognitive decline, but the autonomic dysfunction and specific imaging findings in this case are not characteristic of Late-Onset Tay-Sachs Disease.

rejected.label: Adult Polyglucosan Body Disease
rejected.why: This condition presents with progressive upper and lower motor neuron dysfunction, which is not the primary feature of this case, and the autonomic and imaging findings do not align closely with Adult Polyglucosan Body Disease.

gold: Pseudo-α-galactosidase deficiency (PAGD) syndrome with mild neurocognitive disorder
